[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday meaning: a 'class' is a group of students or a category, and 'public' means open to everyone. Java rule: public class Name { ... } declares the named unit that holds the program's methods; for now S&W say 'class' means 'program'.
[1] misconception (M) -> ClassNameMatchesFile: wrong rule: The class name and the file name are independent. Right rule: public class Name must be saved in a file named Name.java.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> ClassNameMatchesFile: Applies the containment rule unevenly: treats the class's closing brace as the end of main on one trace, or looks for main outside the class on another; the class body is everything between the outermost { and }. (here mixing in: "class name and filename are independent")

[0] names_the_element (N): A class declaration (public class Name { ... }) is the outer container of a Java program; in Chapter 1 each program is a single class with a single method main().
[1] states_the_rule (S): A program is written as public class Name { <method declarations> }; the outermost braces contain the class definition and the inner braces contain the method definitions, and the keywords public and class are required.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): The class declaration itself does not execute: java Name looks up the class Name and calls its main(); the class is just the container that is searched.
[1] output_prediction (OP): A class declaration produces no output; compiling it produces the file Name.class.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Declaring the class changes no variable at run time; it only defines the name (Name) that javac uses for Name.class and that java Name uses to find main.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The name after 'class' must equal the file name without .java.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): main must be declared inside the class's braces; java Name looks only inside class Name for main.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Purpose: package and name a program so it can be compiled and run by name; copying HelloWorld.java and replacing the name on the first line is how a new program is started.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> ClassNameMatchesFile: Renaming the class requires renaming the file (and the java command) to keep it compiling and runnable; moving main outside the class braces breaks compilation.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: public class Name needs the keyword class (and correct spelling). Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: omitting or misspelling class (or public) on the first line
[2] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): In Chapter 1 every program is exactly one public class containing main; a separate class (and file) is needed for each separate program. Multiple classes and methods come only in Section 2.1.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Every { must be matched by a }. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: a missing or extra brace around the class or method body
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A public class must be in a file of the same name. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: class name differs from file name
